title: Charlotte Jackson Fine Art presents Helen Pashgian
summary: An exhibition of works by Helen Pashgian opened at Charlotte Jackson Fine Art on November 6 and remains through December 5, 2026. An opening reception will be held Friday, December 6, 5-7 pm. The gallery is located in the Railyard Arts District at 554 South Guadalupe Street. Have you ever stared into an oncoming ocean wave to see it illuminated, brilliant blue-green, by sunlight pouring through it? That perfectly imperfect and shifting color. That luminous volume of light. But then the vision is gone in an instant - the wave crests, foams, falls. And you are left aching for another vision of pure color. Light pours into Helen Pashgian's resin sculptures. The shape and shine of the spheres seems to somehow bend and hold light, pooling it inside so that they glow from within. title: Opera Gallery Miami pairs Alex Katz and Julian Opie in exhibition
summary: Opera Gallery Miami is pleased to present 'Face to Face', an exhibition bringing together the work of Alex Katz and Julian Opie around one of art's most persistent subjects: the human figure. Through paintings, sculptures and video works, the exhibition considers how each artist simplifies the figure to make it immediate and recognizable. Although their visual languages differ, both artists pare back descriptive detail to focus on the elements that make a figure legible—a face, a gesture, a posture or the outline of a body. Their approaches diverge, however, in what remains: Katz retains the individuality of his subjects, while Opie pushes the figure towards a more universal visual language. title: Gagosian presents Georg Baselitz's final paintings and sculptures in New York
summary: Gagosian is presenting an exhibition of recent work by Georg Baselitz at the 555 West 24th Street gallery in New York. Conceived and designed by the artist and curated by Richard Calvocoressi, Meine Schule is Gagosian’s first presentation of Baselitz’s work since his death in April, and includes his last completed paintings; his last sculpture, Strawinsky (Stravinsky, 2026); and a second late sculpture, 1965 (2024). The November show marks more than twenty-five years of collaboration between the gallery and the artist. Larry Gagosian, in his foreword to the exhibition’s catalogue, notes that the works on view cap a remarkable sixty-year career and represent “a creative goldmine.” Two paintings from the series Meine Schule

title: The Frick Collection presents Kent Monkman paintings inspired by Vermeer
summary: Beginning this fall, The Frick Collection will present an installation in its intimate Cabinet Gallery showcasing a series of new paintings by the Cree artist Kent Monkman (b. 1965), whose practice explores historic European art and narratives from an Indigenous perspective. Monkman takes inspiration from Officer and Laughing Girl (ca. 1657), one of the Frick's three paintings by Johannes Vermeer. Through this series, Monkman expands the histories traditionally associated with such Dutch paintings, highlighting ways in which Vermeer and his contemporaries lived and worked in a context of avid global trade and colonization. With his characteristic humor, style, and deeply researched iconography, Monkman deploys his alter ego—the time-traveling, shapeshifting, gender-fluid Miss Chief Eagle Testickle (a play on the words mischief and egotistical)—to imagine an evolution of Indigenous and European encounters over

title: Hauser & Wirth announces representation of artist rafa esparza
summary: Hauser & Wirth announced worldwide representation of Los Angeles-based artist rafa esparza, in close collaboration with Commonwealth and Council. Since the early 2010s, esparza has drawn on personal narrative, memories and his experience growing up in Los Angeles to weave together emanations of land, migration, desire and belonging in works that are dense and unabashedly sensual. At the center of his practice lies adobe, the traditional earthen building material his father taught him to make. Mixed by hand from loam, straw, water and manure, adobe serves as both the physical matter and conceptual foundation for his sculptures, paintings and installations. title: Roger Dean's original 'Fragile' cover art for Yes emerges after decades missing to make auction debut at Heritage
summary: For decades, Roger Dean’s fantastical world traveled everywhere its original painting could not: onto record shelves, into the hands of millions of listeners and deep into the visual imagination of rock music. Now, the original front cover artwork for Yes’ landmark 1971 album Fragile, recovered and reunited with Dean in September, will make its auction debut at Heritage Auctions on Dec. 2. The painting will be a centerpiece of Heritage’s Nov. 30–Dec. 3 Entertainment & Music Memorabilia Signature® Auction, marking the first time original album cover artwork from Dean’s celebrated 1970s collaboration with Yes has come to auction. Its appearance follows the 55th anniversary of the album’s November 1971 U.K. release. “This is an exceptional piece of music history, not simply because it is the original artwork behind one of the most recognisable album covers of the progressive rock era, but because of the extraordinary

title: Tate Britain celebrates creative partnership of Vanessa Bell and Duncan Grant
summary: Tate Britain celebrates the extraordinary five-decade creative partnership between Vanessa Bell (1879-1961) and Duncan Grant (1885-1978), two of the most influential British artists of the 20th century. Associated with the trailblazing Bloomsbury Group, Bell and Grant’s radical experimentation and unconventional approach to life reshaped art, literature and societal thought in Britain. Featuring over 300 works, Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury is the first major exhibition to chart the duo’s relationship and artistic trajectory – from early post-impressionist and abstract paintings to late naturalistic self-portraits, landscapes and still lifes. Demonstrating how they broke down the boundaries between art and everyday life, the show brings together furniture, ceramics and textiles adorned with their modernist designs, as well as a once-in-a-lifetime restaging of the artists’ studio, relocated to Tate Britain from their East Sussex home, Charleston. title: Albertina presents major retrospective of Austrian artist Arnulf Rainer
summary: Arnulf Rainer numbers among post-1945 Austrian and international art’s most significant and uncompromising personalities. This artist, who was born in Baden (near Vienna) in 1929 and passed away in Upper Austria in late 2025, left an indelible mark on international art history as an innovator who spent over seven decades probing the outer limits of painting. From the very beginning of his artistic career, fired on by his resolute resistance against all of National Socialism’s brutal restrictions, Rainer consistently strove for independence and autonomy. It was with his radical “overpaintings” of the 1950s that he became known internationally and rose to occupy an important place in the post-1945 artistic pantheon. title: Prada presents 'Chuanqi: Spacetime Dialogues' exhibition at Shanghai's Rong Zhai
summary: Prada presents “Chuanqi: Spacetime Dialogues at Rong Zhai,” an exhibition curated by art historian, critic, and curator Wu Hung, bringing together works by four contemporary Chinese artists: Geng Xue, Peng Wei, Song Dong, and Xiaoze Xie. Organized with the support of Fondazione Prada, the project will be on view from 12 November 2026 to 28 February 2027 at Prada Rong Zhai, the historic 1918 residence in Shanghai restored by Prada and reopened to the public in 2017. “Chuanqi: Spacetime Dialogues at Rong Zhai” features a selection of artworks by Geng Xue, Peng Wei, Song Dong, and Xiaoze Xie, creating a dialogue with the interior spaces and layered history of Prada Rong Zhai. The villa’s rooms, once the backdrop for private life, work, conversations, and social gatherings, provide a distinctly intimate setting, unlike a conventional exhibition venue. title: Sotheby's Important Watches sale breaks new records in Geneva
summary: Hot on the heels of delivering the highest total for a watch sale in its history in Hong Kong this September, as well as the most valuable watch auction ever held in Asia, Sotheby's has broken through the $30 million mark with its Important Watches Sale in Geneva. With a total of CHF 26,317,216 / $32,145,128, Sotheby's achieved its strongest live watch auction results in Geneva in more than a decade, accelerating the momentum established by the previous two Important Watches live sales in May 2026 and November 2025, both of which performed exceptionally well. Driven by record participation for a Sotheby's watch auction in Geneva, collectors competed online, by telephone and from a packed saleroom at Geneva's Mandarin Oriental, propelling the average lot value to, nearly $180,000, its highest level ever for a Sotheby's watch auction in Geneva. title: Sarah Morris examines corporate power in new São Paulo exhibition
summary: Fortes D’Aloia & Gabriel presents Lady Snowblood, a new solo exhibition by Sarah Morris, opening November 12 at FDAG Barra Funda. Morris has created a new series of paintings developed in relation to Brazil, the exhibition continues her investigation into the systems, structures, and visual languages through which power organizes contemporary life. The new paintings take as their points of departure corporate entities of both Brazilian and multinational conglomerates such as Palantir, Telefônica, Banco Safra, Ambev, Unilever, Klabin, and Vale. A new form of landscape confronts us. Drawing from the bureaucratic and organizational systems associated with these corporations, Morris creates her own unique language visualizing the networks that span telecommunications, finance, consumer goods, paper production, and mining to name a few. title: Galerie Eva Presenhuber presents Louisa Gagliardi's fifth solo exhibition
summary: Galerie Eva Presenhuber presents Long Distance Relationship, the fifth solo exhibition by Swiss artist Louisa Gagliardi with the gallery. A long-distance relationship thrives on a paradox: one is connected yet separated, feeling close and distant at the same time. Louisa Gagliardi makes this field of tension the theme of her current exhibition. Relationships emerge between the works, to the exhibition visitors, and in the proximity and distance of an immediately lived moment in a changing world with an uncertain future. This multi-layered quality characterizes Louisa Gagliardi’s artistic practice. Her pictures begin on the screen and unfold physically in space. Gagliardi paints digitally, prints the image on PVC, and subsequently works on it with various types of varnish, such as nail polish. The impasto application creates depth and a moment of joyful fascination when the varnish glitters upon observation. Surfaces of captivating ambiguity are created: digital, smooth, and glossy

title: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg exhibits six decades of Danish art and design history
summary: Discover some of the biggest names in Danish art as Kunsten opens the doors to six decades of art history. Encounter works by Anna Ancher, Vilhelm Lundstrøm, Asger Jorn and Wilhelm Freddie, among others, and explore works from Kunsten’s own collection dating from around 1900 to the 1960s. Along the way, you’ll discover some of the artistic movements that transformed art during the first half of the 20th century. From modernism’s fresh approach to colour and form to surrealism’s exploration of the unconscious and the spontaneous, expressive visual language of the CoBrA artists. Bringing together well-known masterpieces and works that are rarely on display, the exhibition offers a broad perspective on a period in which art underwent remarkable changes in just a few decades. v

title: Eunnam Hong explores multiplicity of the self in cinematic paintings at Mendes Wood DM
summary: When Eunnam Hong talks about her work with me her reference points are novels and, especially, movies, not paintings. And this makes perfect sense because, even if hers are not exactly narrative paintings, they are constructed like scenes in a story. Yet when I look at her work, I still find myself thinking intensely about painting. My explanation of the apparent contradiction is this: Painting is a larger and more inclusive art than we are used to imagining it is, and – contrary to the demands of certain theorists – it can encompass means used equally by other arts without sacrificing its aesthetic specificity. title: Heritage Auctions realizes $2.58 million led by record David Bates painting
summary: A record-setting painting by David Bates and a Texas shopper’s extraordinary Goodwill discovery supplied two memorable results as Heritage Auctions’ Nov. 5 Texas & Western Art and Nov. 6 Ethnographic Art auctions brought a combined $2.58 million. Bates’s Sunflowers (2003) led the Texas & Western Art Signature® Auction at $325,000, establishing a new auction record for a painting by the artist and surpassing the previous benchmark Heritage set in 2020. The auction realized $1.93 million across 244 lots, drawing 842 international bidders and achieving a 96% sell-through rate. Sunflowers turns a familiar still-life subject into a commanding presence. Bold outlines, muscular brushwork and strongly constructed forms give the flowers an almost sculptural weight, bringing together Bates’s affinity for nature and his deeply personal approach to painting. “Bates’s Sunflowers encompasses everything collectors love about his work: extraordinary color, a powerful sen

title: Alison Bradley Projects presents first exhibition with textile artist Hiroko Takeda
summary: Alison Bradley Projects presents here is a coast; here is a harbor, the gallery's first exhibition with Japanese-born, New York–based artist Hiroko Takeda (b.1966). Bringing together works spanning different periods of her career, the exhibition traces Takeda's sustained interrogation of weaving as a medium of abstraction, material experimentation, and poetic expression. Drawing upon Japanese craft traditions, twentieth-century modernism, and industrial textile design, Takeda creates compositions in which structural precision and material unpredictability coexist. Through an unconventional vocabulary of natural and synthetic fibers, found materials, and interrupted woven structures, her work considers how personal memory, historical narratives, and the physical world might be registered through thread. title: Rago Wright announces special auction celebrating Lindsey Adelman Studio's 20th anniversary
summary: Rago Wright announced Light Work: Lindsey Adelman Celebrates 20 Years, a special auction commemorating the 20th anniversary of Lindsey Adelman Studio. Featuring forty works spanning two decades of groundbreaking design, the auction brings together archival pieces, one-of-a-kind creations, jewelry, drawings, and prototypes of previously unreleased concepts, offering an intimate look at the evolution of one of contemporary design’s most innovative studios. Since founding her New York studio in 2006, Adelman has challenged the conventions of lighting design, transforming functional objects into expressive sculptural forms. Known for her fearless experimentation with materials, scale, and composition, she has developed a distinctive visual language that blurs the boundaries between art and design. title: Rare Ionia electrum stater leads Heritage's World & Ancient Coins Auction
summary: An extraordinary Ionia electrum stater dating to the late sixth century BC sold for $97,600 to lead Heritage’s Nov. 5–6 World & Ancient Coins Platinum Session and Signature® Auction to $3,378,120. “Prices were strong all across the board, with Indian material bringing some of the strongest prices in the sale, though there are still surprises, like the 1715 Escudo that generated an impressive, record bid of $91,500 ” says Kyle Johnson, Heritage’s Managing Director of World & Ancient Coins. The Ionia electrum stater, one of just three examples of the rare ancient Greek coin identified in sales archives, topped an auction that featured nearly 400 lots spanning centuries of numismatic history. Struck circa 540-500 BC, it features the conjoined foreparts of a bull and roaring lion on the obverse, an unusual composition in which the animals’ forms create a striking optical effect. title: Gooding Christie's sells first Ferrari 499P Modificata at auction
summary: Gooding Christie's, the automotive leg of global luxury market leader Christie's, conducted its first ever Swiss auction as part of Geneva Luxury Week, culminating in an exceptionally strong debut. The first Geneva Auction realized over CHF 21 million, led by the star car, a 2024 Ferrari 499P Modificata – the first of its kind to ever sell at auction for a remarkable price of CHF 8,217,500, and the top-selling car lot at auction in Switzerland this year. Further, Gooding Christie's kicked off their introduction to the Swiss market with a remarkable 96% sell-through rate and an average price of CHF 916,253 per lot sold. Additional high points throughout the evening at the Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues included the record-setting sale of the 2025 Ferrari SF90 XX Spider, sold for CHF 1,580,000, and the incredibly strong sale of the 2018 Lamborghini Aventador SVJ 63, which realized CHF 905,000 after a spirited bidding war led by veteran Gooding Christie's auctioneer Charlie Ross. title: Christie's London presents 'Love & Lust' auction of romantic artifacts
summary: From passionate love letters and iconic cinematic costumes to the objects behind some of the best-loved stories in literature, Love & Lust: A Literary Guide brings together an irresistible selection of works celebrating the many expressions of love, romance and desire. Taking place at Christie's London on 9 December 2026, the live auction comprises approximately 30 books, manuscripts, autograph letters and original works, spanning centuries of passion in cultural history. Few costumes have made quite the impression of the emerald gown (estimate: £100,000–120,000) worn by Keira Knightley as Cecilia Tallis in Atonement. Designed by Jacqueline Durran, the gown has become synonymous with one of cinema's most memorable romantic moments. Adapted from Ian McEwan's acclaimed novel, Joe Wright's 2007 film tells a story of love, jealousy and devastating misunderstanding. title: Acquavella Galleries presents Harumi Klossowska de Rola's New York solo debut
summary: Acquavella Galleries presents Horizon, its first solo exhibition of works by Harumi Klossowska de Rola in New York. Featuring over twenty new and recent sculptures, Horizon continues the artist’s long-standing exploration of the natural world, seeking to capture both its forms and its untamed spirit. Taking wild flora and fauna as her subjects, Klossowska draws inspiration from nature’s immense beauty and ancient histories, inviting us to reconsider mankind’s relationship with the natural world. Though the works on view are all inspired by the trees and animals of the northern regions stretching from the Arctic to British Columbia, the exhibition’s title is universal, reflecting a broader connection with nature. In her work, Klossowska draws upon a wide range of cultural traditions and artistic practices that have long revered animals and the natural world, from Japanese Shintoism to the traditions of First Nations peoples and ancient Egypt. title: Abbas Akhavan's first mid-career survey and first major U.S. show opens at the Walker Art Center
summary: This Fall, the Walker Art Center will open Abbas Akhavan: Variations on a Garden, the artist’s first mid-career survey and his first major exhibition in the United States. Akhavan, who is currently representing Canada at the Venice Biennale, has come to be recognized for his poignant, site-responsive installations, which engage with the histories, architectures, economies, and people of the places he studies. The forthcoming survey features important works from over the past two decades—many to be presented in the U.S. for the first time—providing the first comprehensive view into the arc of his career and the recurring conceptual concerns woven across his distinct projects. Variations on a Garden includes both intimately-scaled sculptural works and ambitious, large-scale installations such as curtain call, variations on a folly (2021), which recreates the colonnade that once led to the ancient Palmyra Arch in Syria. title: Museum Folkwang explores the interconnections between Islamic art and European modernism
summary: With the exhibition Following Damascus … Karl Ernst Osthaus and the Arts of the Islamicate World (6 November 2026 to 21 February 2027), Museum Folkwang is, for the first time, devoting a comprehensive exhibition to the former "Islamic Department" and its legacy within the modern Folkwang universe. Around 340 objects – ranging from ceramics and textiles to metalwork and glassware – provide an insight into the acquisition policy of the museum's founder, Karl Ernst Osthaus (1874–1921), illustrating his perspective on the art of the Islamicate world. From 1898 onwards, even before paintings by Auguste Renoir or Vincent van Gogh found their way into the Museum Folkwang's collection, Osthaus gathered applied arts dating from the 4th to the 19th centuries on his travels through North Africa and West Asia, thereby laying the foundations for the "Islamic Department" of the early Folkwang Museum. title: Museum Angewandte Kunst explores Japanese aesthetic of shibui in new exhibition
summary: The Museum Angewandte Kunst explores a Japanese concept of timeless beauty in its new exhibition, Shibui. An Aesthetic Beyond Cultural Boundaries, part of the meet asian art series. Although deeply rooted in traditional Japanese aesthetics, shibui describes qualities that can also be found in everyday objects and works of art from other cultures. By bringing East Asian and European objects into dialogue, the exhibition shows how this aesthetic transcends geographical and cultural boundaries. This exhibition presents a selection from the extensive Asian collection of the Museum Angewandte Kunst. The objects originate from Japan, China, Korea, and Europe and span approximately two millennia up to the present day. The term shibui can be traced back in the history of Japan to the Muromachi period (1336–1573). Originally, it referred to the bitter, astringent taste of an unripe persimmon.
